newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Bre-X, Barrick agree Busang split.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Bre-X, Barrick agree Busang split.

text.p: Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp. have agreed on a split of the huge Busang gold find in East Kalimantan province, with the Indonesian government getting a 10 percent share, a top mining official said Tuesday.

"The government takes 10 percent. Bre-X will have 22.5 percent and Barrick 67.5 percent," Umar Said, secretary-general of the Mines and Energy Ministry, told Reuters. The find is estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold currently valued around $21 billion.

Umar said the next step for the two companies would be to form a joint venture, opening the way for contracts of work to further explore and develop the property, and to settle disputes with local partners.
A source close to the negotiations between the two companies said the agreement covered the Busang II and III areas of the find, which contain the bulk of the gold.
Bre-X already has a contract of work and a local partner for Busang I, which it estimates contains only about 2.6 million ounces of gold.
Umar said Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana would provide clarifications to certain questions raised by Bre-X and Barrick in a joint submission made to the ministry on Monday.
"We have made a submission ... which says we can work together if the government can satisfy requests by both parties on a couple of items," Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh told Reuters on Monday.
"Within the document, there were certain concerns that we've asked the government to give us guidance on," he said.

The source close to the negotiations told Reuters in Jakarta that Bre-X wanted to clarify the status of its local partner, PT Askatindo Karya Mineral, which has a 10 percent interest in Busang II and III.
"We need to accommodate our Indonesian partner who has a 10 percent stake," the source said.
"This has yet to be resolved," he said when asked if the partner's stake would come from Bre-X's portion.
"He (the partner) has his signature on the contract of work application for Busang II and III which had been initialled and agreed to in principle by the government," the source said.
The application was approved by parliament in July, and by the Investment Ministry in September.
The source said Bre-X and Barrick had reached agreement on financial terms, but declined to say how much Barrick would pay Bre-X for the stake in Busang.
He said Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims to own 40 percent of the Busang property, was not part of the deal on Busang II and III.
"No. This (agreement) only deals with Busang II and III," he said.
Merukh has an undisputed 10 percent stake in Busang I. He could not be reached for comment.
The source said Bre-X also wanted to clarify with the Mines and Energy Ministry the procedures for a joint application with Barrick for a new contract of work for Busang II and III.

"Bre-X is seeking a clarification on how the government wants to implement a new contract of work over an existing one," he said. "Bre-X and Barrick cannot set up a joint venture until there is a clarification from the government."
